newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end touch firmer, Florida frost looms.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end touch firmer, Florida frost looms.

text.p: FCOJ futures ended slightly firmer as the market paused after Wednesday's selloff, but no damage was expected this weekend from the colder weather in Florida's citrus belt, traders and forecasters said.
During this week the market rallied but failed to break the 18-day moving average, and fell back sharply Wednesday before taking a breather Thursday, a trader said.
"I am looking for us to retest the lows again and reach 74.00 cents basis March within a couple of months unless we get some strong weather," the trader added.

Forecaster Jon Davis of Smith Barney said temperatures in the citrus belt over the coming days will be at their coldest on Sunday, with likely widespread frost in the northern areas, and patchy frost in the southern region.
"A frost does not tend to produce any significant damage to the fruit on the trees," Davis said.
In addition, there was no indication that the next surge of cold air, due over the weekend of January 25 to 26, will be extremely intense, Davis added.
March orange juice futures settled 0.65 cent firmer at 80.40 cents per pound, traded narrowly between 80.70 and 80.00 cents. Volume was estimated at 2,500 lots.
